Yes — this gives me exactly the confidence I meant. I clicked "View saved copy" and got a clean, readable version of the page's actual text and image, with the date it was saved and a note of where it originally came from. That's the reassurance I was after: even if that original address dies tomorrow, what I deliberately kept is still right here in front of me, readable. Keeping a tidy reading copy rather than just a fragile link is spot on.

One related thing I want to raise while we're on preserving, since it's the same "it'll still be there" worry: not everything I save is a normal web article. Sometimes it's a PDF — a report or a paper someone linked to. For those, a cleaned-up "reading copy" doesn't really make sense to me; what I'd want is for the app to just hold onto the actual PDF file itself, so I can open the real document later even if the link goes dead. So for a page that's really a PDF, I'd expect the saved copy to *be* that PDF. Could the preserving handle that case too?
